subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should fenced legacy `MEDIA:` directives stay non-extracting with delivery-boundary warnings, be extracted as attachments, or remain documented as by-design only?
rationale: Current parser behavior intentionally preserves fenced examples as text, but the report shows a silent media-delivery failure; choosing extraction versus diagnostics changes the user-visible attachment contract and false-positive behavior.

options.title: Warn At Delivery Boundary
options.body: Keep fenced tokens as text, emit one diagnostic warning only from the outbound delivery path, and review the linked PR after its warning-path repair.

options.title: Extract From Fences
options.body: Treat standalone fenced `MEDIA:` lines as attachments, accepting that code examples can become deliverable media unless additional policy is designed.

options.title: Docs Only
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and rely on documentation that legacy `MEDIA:` lines must be standalone plain text.

recommendation.title: Warn At Delivery Boundary
recommendation.body: Keep fenced tokens as text, emit one diagnostic warning only from the outbound delivery path, and review the linked PR after its warning-path repair.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the live changes-requested review on the linked PR and is already carrying the warning-boundary decision.
